vhs1256.development_object_note: VHS 1256 was seen by the inventor's probe first: a calibration object, not a blind test

blind_scan.method: For every exposure that covers the host, the host's place is predicted from Gaia (proper motion and parallax at the exposure's date). A pixel-integrated Gaussian is fitted in a 7 x 7 pixel box (free flux, x, y, width and background, weights from the pipeline's variance) and the offset from the Gaia place is converted to arcsec East and North with the local WCS. The offsets are grouped by wavelength. The walk is the median offset at 2.9 to 5 micrometres minus the median at 0.75 to 1.65, with 0.04 arcsec added in quadrature to each group for what the astrometry cannot do. Its direction is the companion's position angle. A second fit then adds a companion at that direction, scanning its separation from 2 to 12 arcsec, and the same fit is repeated with the companion turned by 90, 180 and 270 degrees: those controls measure what the extended wings of the image fake. The companion-to-host flux ratio is the fit at the walk direction minus the median of the controls.
cautions: A red background source (galaxy, reddened giant, brown dwarf in the background) walks the image centre exactly as a companion does. Only a common-motion check (an older catalogue position against SPHEREx's) separates a companion from a background source.
Hosts brighter than K about 7 saturate in detectors 1 to 4; hosts fainter than K about 12 give walks too noisy to use.

The fitted centre responds to a neighbour less than the flux-weighted shift. At separations under about 9 arcsec the walk is smaller than ratio x separation; the two-source fit handles this but its ratios are rough, and at 4.4 to 5 micrometres they run 30 to 40 per cent below AllWISE's deblended values on the one test object.
Under about 2.5 arcsec the walk is below the 0.04 arcsec systematic floor for any companion of ordinary contrast: close-in planets are out of reach.
A walk toward a source that Gaia, 2MASS, AllWISE or CatWISE already lists means a known source is the cause; it is not a new finding.
blind_scan.rough_flux_note: rough: net ratio times the host's median flux in the bin; not a calibrated spectrum
